summary: the harness declaration carries `maxEntryDepth`, passed to the chain and read by the package's prompt render and its queue-reading gates alike
acceptance: a declaration naming `maxEntryDepth` reaches `Chain.maxEntryDepth`, the rendered forest rules state that cap, and a package gate's queue parse refuses past it; a declaration naming none leaves every side on the engine's default of four
tests: the rendered entry schema states the declared depth cap
a package gate's queue parse refuses a forest deeper than the declared cap
pins: a declaration naming no maxEntryDepth leaves the engine's default on every side

interface.changes: a declaration may name `maxEntryDepth`; the factory hands it to `Chain.maxEntryDepth`, to the prompt's schema render, and to the package's own queue parses
interface.hides: that the rendered forest rules and the gates' parses are separate reads an author would otherwise have to keep at one value
interface.rejected: leaving the cap to `Chain.maxEntryDepth` alone — a consumer can already set it there, and it moves the parse without moving the rendered rules, telling a producer a bound its own queue read does not keep

notes: `harness/prompts.ts` (`PENDING_SCHEMA`) and the two `parsePendingQueue` calls in `harness/gates.ts` pass no cap today, and the prompt's own comment states the condition this entry closes. The declaration walks in `tests/harnessDeclaration.test.ts` read both doc pages, so a new field reds them until each names it.
